{
  "thinking": "Blank table and ten minutes left. A fish is an easy outline for a judge to read: a closed body with a forked tail. I'll take the pad and sketch it, with the nose as START so every line leaves going right.",
  "say": "I'll grab the pad. Let's do a fish: nose on the left where the start is, body outline going over and under, and a forked tail on the right. Tom, can you take the tail fins once I've drawn them?",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 8,
  "point": [4, 10],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[4, 10], [8, 7], [16, 6], [22, 8], [26, 10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[4, 10], [8, 13], [16, 14], [22, 12], [26, 10]]},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 26, "y0": 10, "x1": 29, "y1": 6},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 26, "y0": 10, "x1": 29, "y1": 14},
    {"type": "label", "x": 7, "y": 9, "text": "eye"}
  ],
  "sketch_clear": false,
  "do": "stop",
  "notes": "Animal: fish facing right. START at nose (4,10). Stroke 1 = top body curve, stroke 2 = bottom body curve (both from START), strokes 3 and 4 = tail fins from the tail joint (26,10). Next: trace stroke 1 and 2 myself, then the fins. Someone needs to watch the start line and check it's connected to the table start."
}
